ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct cream-colored, V-shaped mark between the eyes and possesses prominent, fleshy, triangular toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus pulivijayani* is best distinguished by its unique, significantly elongated third finger, which is notably longer than those of other *Nyctibatrachus* species.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus pulivijayani* inhabits evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats, typically found near rocky stream beds at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Vijayan's Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects along the rocky streams and damp forest floors of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus pulivijayani* breeds during the monsoon, exhibiting direct development where eggs are laid on wet rocks and hatch directly into froglets.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus pulivijayani* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: Vijayan's Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps from damp leaf litter and rocky crevices near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
